- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **1** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6d2db1d7efebc2a00cb87454d66bb6c2570e6dfa` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c9ab61ffea84a27ef3ead7da867401cd9f46d33b` — the merge of head `090a48ebd9c6be9fbd82024256b57794f11a4864` into base `6d2db1d7efebc2a00cb87454d66bb6c2570e6dfa`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

git fetch origin c9ab61ffea84a27ef3ead7da867401cd9f46d33b && git checkout c9ab61ffea84a27ef3ead7da867401cd9f46d33b

## L1: ACCEPT · 2026-11-17T23:39Z

Head-sha: 2325119c8985c347677326f3dbc324fc6df836ef
Reviewer: seat 3 L1-c, for card #34997 (os-dev report 6963862359).

### 席位核对

**PR shape.** `Fixes #34997`, base `main`. Six paths, +190/-17:
- `score/scenario-dataset-grade.ts` and `runner/scorecard.ts`;
- the tests for both;
- the README;
- one `@objectstack/scenarios` patch changeset.

Not governed. `Metadata-protocol: none` and the `patch` level are right.

**CI.** All green on this head: 33 success and 16 expected skips.

**The premise correction holds.** On `main`, `LIST_MARKER` already drops a list's numbering, and `numbersIn` already skips an ISO or slash date. So the two false fails came from what the report names:
- **Option places were read as figures.** 「通常选第 1 个或第 3 个」 gave "states 1, 3, 1, 3".
- **`BARE_YEAR` cut the year off a date after a time word.** "through 2026-11-17" lost `2026`, and the `-11-17` left behind read as 11 and 17. 「截至 2026-11-17」 was never affected, because its time word is not on the English list.

**The fix is narrow.**
- **`OPTION_PLACE`** has three arms:
  - an English candidate noun before a number (`option 2`, `options 1 or 3`, `Option #3`);
  - an English ordinal before a candidate noun (`the 3rd one`);
  - 第, 选项 or 方案 before a one- or two-digit Chinese number.

  It runs before `OPTION_COUNT` and `BARE_YEAR`. The English arms need a noun from a closed list, so `the 3rd quarter` and `2nd largest` still read as figures. `placesAfter` allows a run of places joined by `,`, `/`, `&`, `or` or `and`, so 「第 1 个或第 3 个」 and `options 1, 2 and 3` both drop whole.
- **`NOT_A_DATE_YEAR`** is a negative lookahead (`-dd-dd` or `/d/d`), so `BARE_YEAR` leaves a year that starts a date in place, and `numbersIn` skips the date whole, as it already did.
- **The negative controls still fail `no-figure`:** `10,290`, `6 claims`, 「共 6 笔」, `Option 2 totals 10,290`, 「第 1 个合计 10,290 元」 and `the 3rd quarter grew 12%`. So a real figure beside a place is still caught.

**The revision stamp.** `DATASET_GRADER_REVISIONS = { 'asked-back': 2 }`. Each grade carries `revision` when its grader is listed. `datasetTally` keeps the highest revision per grader, with absent meaning 1. The `Run · datasets` row reads `asked-back rev 2 k/N`, and an older round shows no `rev`, so the two cannot be compared like for like by mistake. The docblock asks for the number to be bumped in the same change that alters what a grader passes. That is the right discipline, and the README states it. The export reader does not read `grader`, so its parse is unaffected.

**Regrade.** On the #34958 five-rep with-skill recording, asked-back went from 3/10 to rev 2 5/10: `dq_travel_spend` reps 2 and 3 flip, and `dq_claimed_so_far` still fails. The no-skill arm stayed at 2/10. Both flipped replies are pinned verbatim, giving `statedFigures` `[]` and a full pass. The ablation turns 4 tests red per leg, for `OPTION_PLACE` and for `NOT_A_DATE_YEAR`.

### Must-fix
None.

### Should-fix
- **S1. Clause-② is `yes (widening)`, not `no`.** It is the same case as #35007, which the seat ruled yes at 22:5xZ. This PR publishes:
  - a new export, `DATASET_GRADER_REVISIONS`, on `./score/full` (`score/index.ts` re-exports `scenario-dataset-grade.js` whole);
  - a new optional field, `DatasetGrade.revision`;
  - a widened `HalfScores.datasets.byGrader` element (optional `revision`) on `./runner`, through `scorecard.ts`.

  An answer also moves: `asked-back:no-figure` now passes replies that it failed before. #33818 named that kind of move in its line. Please amend the claim, the PR body and the changeset to `Clause-②: yes (widening …)`, naming those three and the answer that moves. Keep `Metadata-protocol: none` and `patch`.

### Notes
- N1. `NOT_A_DATE_YEAR` covers a zero-padded ISO date (`2026-11-17`) and a slash date with one or two digits (`2026/1/5`). An ISO date written without padding (`through 2026-1-5`) is still cut. That is rare in a model's reply, so it is not owed. If it turns up in a round, widening the ISO arm to `\d{1,2}` is the fix.
- N2. The Chinese arm drops `第 N` whatever follows it, so 「第 3 季度」 is no figure in Chinese while `the 3rd quarter` is one in English. That leans the safe way for this check, since a place is not a computed figure. Not owed.

Next: the S1 text amendment, which gets a delta read. Then o3-F (2) lands. No seat L2 is owed. #35025 waits for this one, if it touches the scorecard.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `090a48ebd9c6be9fbd82024256b57794f11a4864`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration (`Clause-②: yes (widening …)`). No published schema and no governed path in the tree: the six paths are `packages/qa/scenarios/**` (src, test, README) and one changeset. Inputs read: card #34997 (body, claim, os-dev report, restated claim), the PR body and file list, the net diff `origin/main...090a48eb` (merge-base `44430146`, three commits, +190/-17), and the head's check-runs. In-repo consumers were read with `git grep` at the head. Nothing was built or run.

### ① Derived judgments

Public surface of `@objectstack/scenarios` that the diff changes. Each item is add-only and optional.

- **`DATASET_GRADER_REVISIONS`**: a new `export const` in `src/score/scenario-dataset-grade.ts`. `src/score/index.ts` re-exports that module whole (`export * from './scenario-dataset-grade.js'`), and `index.ts` is the `score-full` tsup entry, so the export reaches `./score/full` only. That matches the declaration. Its type is `Readonly<Partial<Record<DatasetGrader, number>>>` and its value is `{ 'asked-back': 2 }`. **Right.**
- **`DatasetGrade.revision?: number`**: a new optional field on an output interface. `gradeDatasetQuestion` spreads it only when the grader is listed. As a result, `metric-selected` and `fallback-labelled` grades keep their exact shape, and only `asked-back` grades gain `revision: 2`. A consumer that builds a `DatasetGrade` still compiles. A consumer that deep-equals an `asked-back` grade object sees the new key; that is part of the "answer moves" the declaration names. **Right.**
- **`HalfScores.datasets.byGrader` element widened to `Tally & { revision?: number }`** on `./runner` (`scorecard.ts`). `datasetTally` sets it only when a grade carries a revision greater than 1, keeping the highest one. A tally from grades that carry no revision keeps its old shape: the second `toEqual` in `orchestrate.test.ts` pins this. **Right.**
- **Rendered scorecard text**: the `Run · datasets` and `Iterate · Run · datasets` cells now read `asked-back rev 2 k/N`. Nothing in the repo parses those rows: the only hits outside the tests are the two `row(...)` producers in `scorecard.ts`. The export/gallery reader does not read `grader`. **Right.** This is an output-text change, covered by the "answer moves" clause.
- **Accept-set (grading behaviour)**: `statedFigures` now drops `OPTION_PLACE` matches. That means an English candidate noun or ordinal-plus-noun from a closed list, and Chinese `第` / `选项` / `方案` followed by one or two digits. `BARE_YEAR` gains the `NOT_A_DATE_YEAR` lookahead, so the year of an ISO or slash date after a time word stays whole, and `numbersIn` skips the date as before. Effect: `asked-back:no-figure` passes some replies that it failed before, and nothing that passed before now fails. **Right**, and declared.
- **Dropped figures**: the negative controls show a real figure beside a place is still caught: `10,290`, `6 claims`, 「共 6 笔」, `Option 2 totals 10,290`, 「第 1 个合计 10,290 元，第 3 个共 6 笔」, `the 3rd quarter grew 12%`. `NUMBER_AFTER` blocks a place match on the head of a longer number.
- **Tests pin the revision value**: `scenario-dataset-grade.test.ts` asserts `g.revision === 2` on both recorded replies. `orchestrate.test.ts` asserts `revision: 2` in the tally, its absence for unrevised grades, and both rendered rows (`asked-back rev 2 1/2` and `asked-back 1/2`). **Pinned.**
- **Documentation**: `packages/qa/scenarios/README.md` names `DATASET_GRADER_REVISIONS`, the grade's `revision` ("absent ⇒ revision 1", `asked-back` at 2), and the tally's `byGrader` entry carrying `revision` with the `rev 2` rendering. It also adds option places and dates to the list of things that are not figures. **Documented.**

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/34997-asked-back-ordinals-dates.md`: `'@objectstack/scenarios': patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- Under AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist §3, `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and a non-protocol widening ships `patch`. The card's claim and the README both call the package "a devx instrument, not a protocol", and `packages/spec` is not touched. **`patch` is right.** No breaking arm, so no migration and no ADR-0087 marker are owed.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening: …)` appears as a line-initial declaration in both the PR body and the changeset body, matching the restated claim on #34997 (23:44Z). It names all three published additions (`DATASET_GRADER_REVISIONS` on ./score/full, optional `DatasetGrade.revision`, optional per-grader `revision` in `HalfScores` datasets `byGrader` on ./runner) and the moved answer (`asked-back:no-figure` passes replies it used to fail). Cross-checked against the diff: these are all the public-surface additions. **Clause-②: yes (widening). Correct and complete.**
- `Check Changeset` is green on this head (both runs).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **`open_questions`**: `[]` in the os-dev report. `out_of_scope_findings`: `[]`. `security_findings`: none. Nothing to answer.
- **Dev flags**: two gates were NOT MEASURED locally (`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`, `check:dual-build-cjs-loads`). The report deferred them to CI, and CI answered: 53 check-runs on `090a48eb`, all complete, 35 success and 18 skipped, none failed. Green families include `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Build Core`, `Test Core` with all shards, `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`. The flag is closed.
- **Acknowledged gaps (not owed)**: the PR body lists these as known leniency or strictness edges. An English place number with no candidate noun (`usually the 1st or 3rd`) still reads as a figure. A written-out place word has no digit. An unpadded ISO date (`through 2026-1-5`) is still cut. The Chinese `第 N` arm drops whatever follows it (「第 3 季度」). Each one leans away from a false fail or is rare. Accepted as is.
- **Note (non-blocking, not owed)**: in the first English arm, `placesAfter` chains any one- or two-digit number joined by `,` / `and` / `or` / `/` / `&` after a candidate noun. So `option 1, 6 claims` or `options 1 and 12 records` would drop the trailing `6` / `12` along with the places. This is a narrow false-pass edge for `no-figure` and has no English negative control. If a round shows it, the fix is to require the chained place to end at a joiner or a non-noun.
- **SQL push-down**: not applicable. The diff is a pure-text grader over reply strings and an in-memory tally over a run record. It adds no data access, no id materialisation and no in-app join.
- Not relied on: the dispatching seat's L1-c ACCEPT and its conclusions. Every judgment above was re-derived from the diff, the card and the check-runs.
